metadata.title: Symmetry Transition Preserving Chirality in QCD: A Versatile Random Matrix Model

Derivations are in running prose with no proof markers; each proof ends before the sentence that displays the derived formula, so the result is not nested in its own proof.
PRL letter with \paragraph headings only, no \section commands, so every node has an empty section; the key expansion steps are omitted and deferred to a companion paper.
Physics motivation (applications to lattice QCD, condensed matter), the measure/normalization remarks after (3), and the figure caption are not extracted as nodes.

comm.text: We count the number of four-component Dirac fermions by $N_{\rm f}$. In 3d, it is equivalent to $2N_{\rm f}$ two-component Dirac fermions.

nodes.name: Altland-Zirnbauer classification (ten symmetry classes)
nodes.statement: There are just ten symmetry classes of Hermitian operators (including RMT) as proven by Altland and Zirnbauer~\cite{AltZirn}.
conclusions: There are just ten symmetry classes of Hermitian operators (including RMT)

nodes.name: Chiral random matrix model interpolating chGUE and GUE
nodes.statement: In the present work we wish to consider the chiral random matrix \begin{equation} \begin{split} \mathcal{D} =\left(\begin{array}{cc} 0 & iW \\ iW^\dagger & 0 \end{array}\right), ~ W= H_1+i\mu H_2,\\ H_1,H_2\in{\rm Herm}(N)\ \text{and}\ \mu\in[0,1]~~~ \end{split} \end{equation} distributed as \begin{equation} P(\mathcal{D})= \frac{1}{2^N \pi^{N^2}}\exp\left[-\frac{1}{2}\text{tr}(H_1^2+H_2^2)\right]. \end{equation} Here ${\rm Herm}(N)$ denotes the set of Hermitian $N\times N$ matrices.
nodes.statement_short: Chiral block matrix with off-diagonal block $W=H_1+i\mu H_2$, $H_1,H_2$ Gaussian Hermitian.

nodes.name: Chiral random matrix $\mathcal{D}$
nodes.statement: \begin{split} \mathcal{D} =\left(\begin{array}{cc} 0 & iW \\ iW^\dagger & 0 \end{array}\right), ~ W= H_1+i\mu H_2,\\ H_1,H_2\in{\rm Herm}(N)\ \text{and}\ \mu\in[0,1]~~~ \end{split}
nodes.label: RMT-model

nodes.name: Gaussian distribution of $\mathcal{D}$
nodes.statement: P(\mathcal{D})= \frac{1}{2^N \pi^{N^2}}\exp\left[-\frac{1}{2}\text{tr}(H_1^2+H_2^2)\right].
nodes.label: distribution

nodes.name: Partition function with $N_f$ dynamical quarks
nodes.statement: The partition function with $N_{\rm f}$ dynamical quarks with masses $m_1,\ldots,m_{N_{\rm f}}$ is then given by \begin{equation} Z_N^{(N_f)} = \int d\mathcal{D} P(\mathcal{D})\prod_{f=1}^{N_{\rm f}}\det(m_f \mathbb{1}_{2N} +\mathcal{D})\,. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Partition function: average of product of mass determinants over the ensemble.

nodes.name: Partition function $Z_N^{(N_f)}$
nodes.statement: Z_N^{(N_f)} = \int d\mathcal{D} P(\mathcal{D})\prod_{f=1}^{N_{\rm f}}\det(m_f \mathbb{1}_{2N} +\mathcal{D})\,.
nodes.label: eq:0Zdef

nodes.name: Interpolation between GUE and chGUE
nodes.statement: For varying $\mu$ the level statistics of $\mathcal{D}$ interpolates between GUE \cite{Verbaarschot:1994ip,Mehta_book} at $\mu=0$ and chGUE~\cite{Shuryak:1992pi,Verbaarschot:1993pm,Mehta_book} at $\mu=1$.
conclusions: the level statistics of $\mathcal{D}$ interpolates between GUE \cite{Verbaarschot:1994ip,Mehta_book} at $\mu=0$ and chGUE~\cite{Shuryak:1992pi,Verbaarschot:1993pm,Mehta_book} at $\mu=1$

nodes.name: Matrix dimension as spacetime volume
nodes.statement: The random matrix $\mathcal{D}$ replaces the Euclidean Dirac operator in QCD and its matrix dimension $N$ plays the role of the spacetime volume which will be eventually taken to infinity, keeping $Nm_f^2$ and $N\mu^2$ fixed.

nodes.name: Dimensional reduction at high temperature
nodes.statement: It is well known~\cite{Ginsparg:1980ef,Nadkarni:1982kb} that gauge theories at high temperature undergoes dimensional reduction.

nodes.name: chGUE to GUE crossover in high-temperature 4d QCD
nodes.statement: We conjecture a crossover transition of the spectral statistics of the smallest eigenvalues of the Dirac operator from chGUE (4d) to GUE (3d).
conclusions: a crossover transition of the spectral statistics of the smallest eigenvalues of the Dirac operator from chGUE (4d) to GUE (3d)

nodes.name: Euclidean Lagrangian of 3d QCD at finite isospin chemical potential
nodes.statement: The Euclidean Lagrangian is given by \begin{equation} \begin{split} \mathcal{L} = & \overline{\psi}\bigl(\mathcal{D}_{\rm 3d} + \mu_{\rm I} \sigma_3\tau_3+{\rm diag}(m_{\rm u},m_{\rm d})+j\tau_1\bigl)\psi, \end{split} \end{equation} where $\mathcal{D}_{\rm 3d}$ is the 3d Dirac operator which is anti-Hermitian, $\psi$ the two-flavor quark fields, $\mu_{\rm I}$ the isospin chemical potential, $m_{\rm u/d}$ the quark masses, $j$ the source term for the pion condensate, and $\tau_j$ and $\sigma_3$ the Pauli matrices in flavour space and spinor space, respectively.
nodes.statement_short: Two-flavor 3d QCD Lagrangian with isospin chemical potential, quark masses and pion source $j$.

nodes.name: 3d QCD Lagrangian at finite isospin
nodes.statement: \begin{split} \mathcal{L} = & \overline{\psi}\bigl(\mathcal{D}_{\rm 3d} + \mu_{\rm I} \sigma_3\tau_3+{\rm diag}(m_{\rm u},m_{\rm d})+j\tau_1\bigl)\psi, \end{split}
nodes.label: Lag-phys

nodes.name: Matrix model for 3d QCD at finite isospin chemical potential
nodes.statement: One can model this system by the two-matrix model \eqref{eq:0Zdef} with $N_{\rm f}=1$, in close analogy to the 4d case \cite{Osborn:2004}.

nodes.name: Elliptic Ginibre ensemble
nodes.statement: The random matrix $W$ is also known as the elliptic Ginibre ensemble~\cite{Fyodorov:1997,Akemann:2001bf,Akemann:2007rf} and was studied in the scattering at disordered/chaotic systems~\cite{Fyodorov:1997b} as well as in 3d QCD at finite baryon chemical potential~\cite{Akemann:2001bf,Akemann:2007rf}.

nodes.name: Level density vanishes at the origin
nodes.statement: The microscopic level density will always drop to zero at the origin as long as $\mu\neq0$, see Fig.~\ref{fig.microlevel}.
conclusions: The microscopic level density will always drop to zero at the origin

nodes.name: Partially quenched partition function $Z_N^{(k,N_f+k)}$
nodes.statement: To this aim, we consider the partition function involving $k$ bosonic quarks and $N_{\rm f}+k$ fermionic quarks \begin{equation} Z_N^{(k,N_{\rm f}+k)} = \int d\mathcal{D} P(\mathcal{D})\frac{\prod_{j=1}^{N_{\rm f}+k}\det(\kappa_{{\rm f}, j} \mathbb{1}_{2N}+\mathcal{D})}{\prod_{j=1}^{k}\det(\kappa_{{\rm b}, j} \mathbb{1}_{2N}+\mathcal{D})}, \end{equation} with $k=0$ for the ordinary fermionic partition function and $k=1$ and $N_{\rm f}=0$ for the quenched microscopic level density.
nodes.statement_short: Ratio of $N_f+k$ fermionic to $k$ bosonic determinants averaged over the ensemble.

nodes.name: Partially quenched partition function
nodes.statement: Z_N^{(k,N_{\rm f}+k)} = \int d\mathcal{D} P(\mathcal{D})\frac{\prod_{j=1}^{N_{\rm f}+k}\det(\kappa_{{\rm f}, j} \mathbb{1}_{2N}+\mathcal{D})}{\prod_{j=1}^{k}\det(\kappa_{{\rm b}, j} \mathbb{1}_{2N}+\mathcal{D})},
nodes.label: eq:Zval

nodes.name: Source variables $\kappa$
nodes.statement: The source variables are $\kappa=\text{diag}(\kappa_{\rm b};\kappa_{\rm f})=\text{diag}((L\varepsilon-i\lambda_{\rm b})\mathbb{1}_k;(L\varepsilon-i\lambda_{\rm f})\mathbb{1}_k,m_1,\ldots,m_{N_{\rm f}})$ with $m_j$ the masses of the dynamical quarks, $L=\pm1$ the sign of the regularization $\varepsilon>0$ and $\lambda_{\rm b/f}$ the source variables for generating the level density.
nodes.statement_short: Diagonal source matrix with regularized level-density sources and quark masses.

nodes.name: Superspace representation of the partition function
nodes.statement: \begin{split} Z_N^{(k,N_{\rm f}+k)} = \; &\frac{1}{\pi^{2 Nk}}\int dV \exp\big[\! -L\; \text{Str}\,V^\dagger V\kappa \\ &-\text{Str} (V^\dagger V\tau_1)^2/2-\mu^2\text{Str} (V^\dagger V\tau_2)^2/2 \big]. \end{split}
nodes.label: susy:partiton

nodes.name: Suppressed tensor notation in superspace
nodes.statement: Note that we suppress the tensor notation with identity matrices meaning $\kappa$ has to be understood in the $(2k|2N_{\rm f}+2k)$ dimensional superspace as $\kappa\otimes\mathbb{1}_2$ and the Pauli matrices $\tau_j$ as $\mathbb{1}_{k|N_{\rm f}+k}\otimes\tau_j$.

nodes.name: Superbosonization supermatrix $U'$
nodes.statement: In the next step we apply the superbosonization formula~\cite{Zirnbauer:2006,Kieburg:2008} and replace \begin{equation} LV^\dagger V\tau_1\rightarrow \sqrt{N} U'=\sqrt{N}\left(\begin{array}{cc} U'_{\rm bb} & \eta^\dagger \\ \eta & U'_{\rm ff} \end{array}\right), \end{equation} where the the boson-boson block $U'_{\rm bb}$ satisfies $LU'_{\rm bb}\tau_1=(LU'_{\rm bb}\tau_1)^\dagger>0$ and the fermion-fermion block $U'_{\rm ff}$ is unitary. The $2k\times(2k|2N_{\rm f}+2k)$ off-diagonal block $\eta$ comprises only independent complex Grassmann variables.
nodes.statement_short: Replace $LV^\dagger V\tau_1$ by $\sqrt{N}U'$ with positive boson block, unitary fermion block, Grassmann off-diagonal $\eta$.

nodes.name: Superbosonization replacement
nodes.statement: LV^\dagger V\tau_1\rightarrow \sqrt{N} U'=\sqrt{N}\left(\begin{array}{cc} U'_{\rm bb} & \eta^\dagger \\ \eta & U'_{\rm ff} \end{array}\right),

nodes.name: Partition function as supermatrix integral over $U'$
nodes.statement: \begin{split} Z_N^{(k_{\rm b},k_{\rm f})} \propto& \int d\tilde{\mu}(U')\; \text{Sdet}^{N}U' \exp\big[\!-\text{Str}\,U'\widehat{\kappa}\tau_1 \\ & - N\, \text{Str}\,{U'}^2/2 + \widehat{\mu}^2\text{Str} (U'\tau_3)^2/2 \big]. \end{split}
nodes.label: susy:partiton.b

nodes.name: Epsilon-regime rescaling
nodes.statement: Here we have already chosen the rescaling from the $\varepsilon$-regime, namely $\widehat{\kappa}=\sqrt{N}\kappa$ and $\widehat{\mu}^2=N\mu^2$ which are fixed in the large-$N$ limit.

nodes.name: Saddle-point derivation of the chiral Lagrangian
nodes.statement: First we want to consider the partition function with $N_{\rm f}$ dynamical quarks, i.e. $k=0$ \cite{comm}. There is no supersymmetry and the whole supermatrix consists of the fermion-fermion block, only, $U'=U_{\rm ff}$. For $N\to\infty$ we have to solve the saddle point equation \begin{equation} U'^2=\mathbb{1}_{2N_{\rm f}}. \end{equation} This implies that all eigenvalues of $U'$ are $\pm1$. When diagonalizing $U'$ to its eigenvalues $e^{i \phi}=\text{diag}(e^{i \phi_1},\ldots,e^{i \phi_{N_{\rm f}}})$ we would obtain the Vandermonde term $|\Delta_{N_{\rm f}}(e^{i \phi})|^2=\prod_{a<b}|e^{i \phi_b}-e^{i \phi_a}|^2$ as the Jacobian. This term algebraically suppresses all solutions of~\eqref{sad.eq} in $1/N$ which do not have an equal number of $\pm1$. Thus we integrate only over the coset ${\rm U}(2N_{\rm f})/[{\rm U}(N_{\rm f})\times {\rm U}(N_{\rm f})]$ which is the same as for $\mu=0$ (GUE, 3d QCD), see~\cite{Verbaarschot:1994ip}. This coset can be parametrized as $U'=U\tau_3 U^\dagger$ with $U\in{\rm U}(2N_{\rm f})$.
nodes.statement_short: Large-$N$ saddle point $U'^2=1$; the Vandermonde Jacobian selects equal numbers of $\pm1$, reducing to the coset $U(2N_f)/[U(N_f)\times U(N_f)]$.

nodes.name: Restrict to $k=0$
nodes.statement: First we want to consider the partition function with $N_{\rm f}$ dynamical quarks, i.e. $k=0$ \cite{comm}. There is no supersymmetry and the whole supermatrix consists of the fermion-fermion block, only, $U'=U_{\rm ff}$.
nodes.statement_short: Specialize to $k=0$: only the fermion-fermion block remains.

nodes.name: Saddle point equation
nodes.statement: For $N\to\infty$ we have to solve the saddle point equation \begin{equation} U'^2=\mathbb{1}_{2N_{\rm f}}. \end{equation} This implies that all eigenvalues of $U'$ are $\pm1$.
nodes.statement_short: Large-$N$ saddle point forces eigenvalues $\pm1$.

nodes.name: Vandermonde suppression
nodes.statement: When diagonalizing $U'$ to its eigenvalues $e^{i \phi}=\text{diag}(e^{i \phi_1},\ldots,e^{i \phi_{N_{\rm f}}})$ we would obtain the Vandermonde term $|\Delta_{N_{\rm f}}(e^{i \phi})|^2=\prod_{a<b}|e^{i \phi_b}-e^{i \phi_a}|^2$ as the Jacobian. This term algebraically suppresses all solutions of~\eqref{sad.eq} in $1/N$ which do not have an equal number of $\pm1$.
nodes.statement_short: Vandermonde Jacobian suppresses unbalanced saddle points in $1/N$.

nodes.name: Coset integration
nodes.statement: Thus we integrate only over the coset ${\rm U}(2N_{\rm f})/[{\rm U}(N_{\rm f})\times {\rm U}(N_{\rm f})]$ which is the same as for $\mu=0$ (GUE, 3d QCD), see~\cite{Verbaarschot:1994ip}. This coset can be parametrized as $U'=U\tau_3 U^\dagger$ with $U\in{\rm U}(2N_{\rm f})$.
nodes.statement_short: Integrate over coset parametrized by $U'=U\tau_3U^\dagger$.

nodes.name: Chiral Lagrangian / large-N partition function with $N_f$ flavors
nodes.statement: Z^{(0,N_{\rm f})}=\!\!\!\!\! \int\limits_{\text{U}(2N_{\rm f})} \!\!\!\!\!\! d\mu(U)\exp\left[\text{tr}\,U\tau_3U^\dagger \widehat{\kappa}\tau_1-\frac{\widehat{\mu}^2}{2}\text{tr}(U\tau_3U^\dagger\tau_3)^2\right]\!.
nodes.statement_short: Large-$N$ partition function is a $U(2N_f)$ integral with mass term plus a $\widehat{\mu}^2$ symmetry-breaking term.
nodes.label: k-flav-f

nodes.name: Chiral Lagrangian reproduces QCD epsilon-expansion
nodes.statement: We expect that the result \eqref{k-flav-f} reproduces the leading order of the $\varepsilon$-expansion in QCD for the three areas of applications discussed above.
conclusions: the result \eqref{k-flav-f} reproduces the leading order of the $\varepsilon$-expansion in QCD for the three areas of applications discussed above

nodes.name: Pfaffian evaluation of the flavor integral
nodes.statement: In~\cite{Kanazawa:2018b} we have even carried out the integral over $U$ explicitly, which yielded either an $N_{\rm f}\times N_{\rm f}$ or an $(N_{\rm f}+1)\times(N_{\rm f}+1)$ Pfaffian determinant, depending on whether $N_{\rm f}$ is even or odd, respectively.
conclusions: either an $N_{\rm f}\times N_{\rm f}$ or an $(N_{\rm f}+1)\times(N_{\rm f}+1)$ Pfaffian determinant, depending on whether $N_{\rm f}$ is even or odd, respectively

nodes.name: Supersymmetric derivation of the quenched microscopic level density
nodes.statement:
Next we want to derive the microscopic level density in the quenched limit. nodes.name: Non-uniform GUE limit at the origin
nodes.statement: Due to the preservation of chirality in our model, the GUE limit ($\widehat{\mu}\to0$) is not uniform about the origin while it is in~\cite{Damgaard:2010cz,Akemann:2011} when the quark mass vanishes.
assumptions: Due to the preservation of chirality in our model
conclusions: the GUE limit ($\widehat{\mu}\to0$) is not uniform about the origin

nodes.name: Linear level repulsion from the origin
nodes.statement: As we have already pointed out, an exact chirality yields for a complex matrix a linear level repulsion from the origin, though the range where this is happening is of order $\mathcal{O}(\widehat{\mu})$ for small $\widehat{\mu}$.
conclusions: a linear level repulsion from the origin
the range where this is happening is of order $\mathcal{O}(\widehat{\mu})$ for small $\widehat{\mu}$

nodes.name: Suppressed oscillations and uniform chGUE limit
nodes.statement: The oscillations are increasingly suppressed when $\widehat{\mu}$ decreases, whereas the limit $\widehat{\mu}\to\infty$ to the chGUE result is uniformly approached.
conclusions: The oscillations are increasingly suppressed when $\widehat{\mu}$ decreases
the limit $\widehat{\mu}\to\infty$ to the chGUE result is uniformly approached

nodes.name: No difference in bulk and soft-edge statistics
nodes.statement: However we do not expect any differences for the spectral statistics in the bulk and at the soft edges.
conclusions: we do not expect any differences for the spectral statistics in the bulk and at the soft edges

nodes.name: Pfaffian point process at finite N
nodes.statement: In~\cite{Kanazawa:2018a} we have shown that the spectral statistics describe a Pfaffian point process meaning that all $k$-point correlation functions as well as averages over ratios of characteristic polynomials of the random matrix $\mathcal{D}$ are given by Pfaffian determinants which only comprise three functions.
conclusions: the spectral statistics describe a Pfaffian point process meaning that all $k$-point correlation functions as well as averages over ratios of characteristic polynomials of the random matrix $\mathcal{D}$ are given by Pfaffian determinants which only comprise three functions

nodes.name: QCD infrared Dirac eigenvalues follow the Pfaffian point process
nodes.statement: In particular the statistics of the infra-red eigenvalues of the physical Dirac operators in QCD (say 3d staggered Dirac operators or 3d continuum theory with isospin chemical potential) should also follow this Pfaffian point process and all the consequences related to it.
conclusions: should also follow this Pfaffian point process and all the consequences related to it
